purpose: Resolve the first post-visual recontact attempt, execute the first Branch land-based night maritime strike, and update Japanese knowledge of the multi-group US approach without granting automatic carrier hits.
authority_note: CURRENT authority remains 1944-01-01. This is a working event chain only.
historical_sanity_anchors: Historical GALVANIC saw trained Japanese Betty night-torpedo attacks from the Marshalls; US forces also began developing radar/night-fighter countermeasures after those attacks.

Historical FLINTLOCK fast carriers approached through squalls and overcast and achieved near-complete tactical surprise; Branch submarine/contact fusion removes complete surprise but does not remove weather or US radar/CAP.

Historical late-Jan Marshall OOB contained 752nd/753rd land-attack aircraft at Roi/Taroa and 531st carrier-attack aircraft at Wotje; Branch uses these only as type/location anchors and retains its already-closed serviceable totals.

events.event: Two follow-up air searches probe the 10:25-10:45 visual contact motion cone. Weather, US CAP and local course changes deny a second firm visual.
events.effect: Track uncertainty expands, but submarine/DF fusion prevents the operational picture from resetting to zero.

events.event: An inner fast-reposition submarine, moved onto the time-stamped corridor, obtains a strong multi-shaft hydrophone picture and a brief surface/periscope-assisted night observation through squall gaps.
events.report: Large fast formation; heavy escort; course broadly N/NE with tactical zig-zag; speed about 20-23 kt; position error roughly 12-20 nmi; carrier identity not visually re-confirmed.
events.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH same fast-carrier-group track; fresh enough for an area-search night strike, not a precision firing solution.
events.submarine_action: Report/shadow priority is retained over a poor torpedo shot. US ASW later forces the boat deep and breaks continuous contact; no submarine weapon release is credited.

events.event: Marshall air command authorizes a limited night maritime strike from the already-counted Roi/Taroa land-attack pool.
events.package: 8 G4M-class land-attack aircraft launch centered, with torpedo load and one aircraft performing pathfinder/illumination/search-lead duties within the formation. No new aircraft are spawned.
events.guard: This is a limited attack by crews judged night-capable after GALVANIC experience, not the entire land-attack inventory.

events.event: The Japanese raid enters the predicted search box. US radar pickets and post-GALVANIC night-defense procedures detect the approach early enough to vector an ad-hoc night CAP and maneuver the carrier formation.

outcome.near_result: Several torpedoes are released against outer-screen/large-ship silhouettes; no carrier or escort hit is centered. One close pass forces radical maneuver but causes no structural damage.

events.meaning: The Branch information system is good enough to create a real pre-strike attack opportunity, but US radar/night defense and weather still make night torpedo conversion difficult.

events.event: Japanese searches continue on narrowed arcs. A Roi-centered fast reconnaissance sortie obtains a short visual on a second US carrier task group during the afternoon and transmits before being driven off.
events.report: Probable three flight decks with heavy battleship/escort screen; separate from the group seen on 31 Jan. Exact total TF58 remains unknown.
events.parallel_submarine_picture: A separate submarine/logistics report confirms major assault/transport echelons converging on the Kwajalein axis.
events.Japan_knowledge: HIGH multi-TG carrier operation; HIGH amphibious operation; HIGH Kwajalein/Roi primary objective; total US fast decks still underestimated/uncertain.

US_adaptation: Carrier groups treat tactical surprise as compromised and maintain high CAP/radar/ASW readiness.
Night-defense doctrine learned after GALVANIC is spread task-force-wide; it is not treated as an Enterprise-only capability in Branch B.
First suppression strike remains scheduled for the early edge of the 2-4 Feb window rather than being delayed by the failed Japanese raid.
Japan_adaptation: Do not repeat the 31-Jan night attack without a fresh contact; preserve remaining night-qualified crews.
Keep Taroa/Roi aircraft dispersed and staged; radar/plot/radio teams remain at full battle stations.
Use the second carrier-group visual and assault-force reports to update submarine corridors and first-line-carrier threat posture, not to infer the full 11-deck US OOB.
